correctness.rationale: Exact multiplier identity yields global amplitude monotonicity. Stable geometric memory filter proves both-state convergence at equality. A dominated-convergence convolution comparison uses sqrt(beta)<rho<1, then reciprocal increments yield the exact n^-1 amplitude constant and the universal n^-2 memory constant. Separate finite-hit orbits are handled. The embedded checker replays exact identities and five representative finite experiments; finite testing is not substituted for the analytic argument.

originality.rationale: The closest original work proves global convergence strictly below the threshold, instability strictly above it and bounded trapping at equality, but not the critical equality-step global convergence or rate. Other inspected RMSProp stability/rate results impose strict steps. Semantic searches found only nonimplicative adaptive-optimizer parallels; priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Earlier unpublished or poorly indexed marginal-convergence results could contain an equivalent statement; database search alone cannot establish historical priority.

value.rationale: The precise equality case h=2epsilon/a is the natural missing stability boundary between strict global convergence and strict instability in the 2026 motivating work. A complete global dichotomy and exact polynomial decay exponents are mathematically motivated, with surprising beta-independent constants and curvature-independent leading memory amplitude. It is not a numerical gain, arbitrary parameter slice, or renaming of an interior contraction theorem.
